title: Microbatch saturation detection and gradual backpressure projection
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: under unpredictable high QPS bursts we observe microbatch saturation where batch fill stalls, KV cache eviction spikes, and GPU memory headroom drops leading to tail latency regressions and occasional OOM-near behavior. Existing threshold heuristics are brittle: fixed limits either underutilize GPUs or cause abrupt hard-throttles that spike 99th-percentile latency for high-priority customers. Goal: implement a stable, continuous mechanism that detects imminent saturation and applies gradual, model-aware backpressure projections rather than binary throttles. The mechanism should be safe to roll out incrementally, explainable to customers, and able to suggest alternative mitigations (quantized variants, re-routing to dedicated capacity).
motivation: Reduce p99 latency regressions during bursts while preserving throughput and avoiding sudden client errors. Improve predictability of admission decisions and provide clear instrumentation for on-call and customers.
design_proposal: 1) Saturation signal: compute a composite score per serving pool that combines (a) GPU headroom percentile (memory free relative to configured safety margin), (b) KV cache eviction rate (evictions/sec normalized by requests/sec), and (c) microbatch fill slowdown (delta between expected microbatch fill time and observed). Each signal is smoothed with an EMA (alpha configurable). 2) Projection: convert composite score into a continuous admission probability p in (0,1] using a monotonic mapping (logistic-like curve with configurable knee). 3) Priority-aware admission: multiply p by request-priority weights (e.g., reserved dedicated traffic gets higher weight) and by customer SLAs. 4) Gradual backpressure: use probabilistic admission instead of hard drops. For denied requests, optionally return a retry-after header or route to a fallback model/region. 5) Safe-fallback policy: when composite score crosses critical threshold, start warm-up of quantized variant and redirect low-priority traffic gradually. 6) Telemetry: emit per-model and per-pool metrics for composite_score, admission_p, rejected_by_prob, fallback_routed_count, kv_eviction_rate, gpu_headroom_p50/p95/p99, microbatch_fill_ms distribution. 7) Config: per-pool knobs for sensitivity, knee, minimum guaranteed admission for reserved tenants, and safe cap for rejected rate per-minute.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for heavy-burst synthetic load improves by at least 30% in staging compared to current fixed-threshold controller
No customer-facing 5xx increase in canary group after 72h; rejected_by_prob <= 2% for P0 traffic
Composite score and admission_p appear on runtime dashboard with 1s resolution; alerts fire when composite_score > configured-critical for >15s
Fallback routing to quantized model reduces memory pressure by >= 20% for routed fraction
End-to-end tests for admission controller, projection mapping, and fallback routing added to CI
implementation_steps: Prototype composite score computation as a feature-flagged metric in the serving runtime (Rust component) with test harness to replay production traces
Add admission probability module: mapping function + per-pool config stored in config service; default knee tuned from historical traces
Implement probabilistic admission API and retry header semantics in request path; ensure deterministic decision for A/B reproducibility via request-scoped RNG seed
Hook fallback routing to model-routing service with graceful warmup (pre-load quantized model into pool) and circuit-breaker guard
Add necessary telemetry (metrics, histogram labels) and dashboards in Console; add alerting rules for composite_score and rejected_by_prob
Run staged canary: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% of non-reserved traffic with automated rollback on failure criteria
Post-canary: run 48h synthetic QPS spike experiments in dedicated staging cluster and gather memory/KV/latency traces
Ship runtime config knobs and docs; partner with Solutions/SEs to communicate any default behavioral changes to customers
technical_notes:
- Composite score components and mapping must be cheap: compute inside runtime hot path with <200ns overhead per request aggregated via sampling.
- Use exponential decay windows for eviction-rate smoothing to react within ~10s but avoid jitter.
- Admission decisions must be stable across retried requests: tag retry attempts and avoid infinite retry loops.
- Prefer probabilistic admission over token-bucket hard-rejects to maintain soft QoS.
- GPU headroom calculation must account for multi-tenant memory reservations and pinned KV cache memory.
- If headroom falls below emergency margin, trigger immediate conservative AC that only allows reserved SLA traffic and control-plane ops.
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping function edge cases, integration test with synthetic KV eviction generator, e2e load test in staging using locust to simulate bursty QPS with mixed request sizes, fault injection tests for model warmup failures and simulated OOM, and long-running soak with production-like trace replay to validate EMA tuning.
metrics_and_observability: Emit metrics: runtime.composite_score{pool,model}, runtime.admission_p{pool,model}, runtime.rejected_by_prob{pool,model,priority}, kv.evictions_per_sec{pool,model}, gpu.headroom_bytes{pool}, microbatch.fill_time_ms{pool,model}. Create dashboard panels for p95/p99 latency overlayed with composite_score and kv_eviction_rate, and heatmap of admission_p across pools. Add logging for decisions aggregated to avoid high-cardinality logs.
rollout_plan: Feature flag gate, canary rollout to non-reserved traffic only, automated rollback triggers (increase in 5xx, p99 regression >10% versus baseline, rejected_by_prob breach for reserved traffic), staged increase over 7 days with continuous monitoring, and post-mortem within 72h if rollback occurs.
open_questions: What default knee value balances throughput vs tail-latency across our largest pools? (need historical trace sweep)
Should we integrate an offline RL tuning loop to auto-adjust mapping per-pool based on observed SLA tradeoffs?
How to surface admission decisions to customers in the Console without exposing too much internal noise?
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: probabilistic admission may increase client-side retries causing amplified load. Mitigation: add retry-after semantics and client SDK guidance; collaborate with SDK team to interpret headers and back off.
Risk: miscalibrated mapping could starve low-priority but important auxiliary traffic. Mitigation: per-pool minimum guarantees and staged canary with business-owner signoff.
Risk: additional CPU overhead in hot path. Mitigation: sample decisions at sub-100% rate during initial rollout and measure overhead; fall back to aggregated controller if needed.
